The video shows 19-year-old mother Asha with her newborn calf at their enclosure after Asha had been pregnant for 15 months. Keepers said both rhinos were in good health and the birth was an important step in the conservation of the threatened species. Tom Garland from the rhino team at Chester Zoo said the calf was the fourth born to Asha and father Beni, who died earlier this year following a short and sudden illness. "It's always exciting to welcome a new calf and Asha has been a brilliant mum to all her youngsters," he said. "Every birth is important for the future of this species and it's wonderful to see another healthy arrival." The species was driven to near-extinction in the early 1900s by habitat loss and trophy hunting and remains vulnerable to extinction with around 4,000 greater one-horned rhinos living in the wetlands, forests and grasslands of India and Nepal.

Speaking to the media ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix at Losail, the four-time world champion was asked what a "pure" Formula 1 looks like - and whether F1 should lean on DRS, overtake modes, or push-to-pass once the current rules cycle wraps up.
